apps/desktop/build/installer.nsh.content: The return value of `nsDialogs::Create` is popped into `$Dialog` but never validated. On failure `nsDialogs::Create` pushes the literal string `error`, and the script continues, creating the label on an invalid/nonexistent dialog and then calling `nsDialogs::Show` — producing a silently broken page or a hard crash instead of a clean abort. Guard against the `error` sentinel before proceeding.

The label is given a fixed height of `60u`, but the text is ~350 characters. At the default dialog width this needs many more lines than 60 pixels can render, so the firewall/microphone/Bluetooth guidance will be visually truncated and the user will miss part of the security instructions. Increase the control height (or the label should wrap over the full available area) so the full text is visible.

apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts.content: The `unknown-channel` guard is ineffective because `channels` is a plain object literal, so a bracketed lookup resolves inherited `Object.prototype` members. Calling `invoke("constructor")`, `invoke("toString")`, `invoke("valueOf")`, `invoke("__proto__")`, etc. returns a truthy inherited value, so `!ch` is `false` and the intended `unknown-channel` error is never thrown; execution then falls through to `ch.request.parse`, which throws an untyped `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parse')`. Use an own-property check instead.
apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts.suggestion_code:
if (!Object.hasOwn(channels, channel)) throw new Error(`unknown-channel: ${channel}`);
    const ch = channels[channel as Channel];
apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts.existing_code:
const ch = channels[channel as Channel];
    if (!ch) throw new Error(`unknown-channel: ${channel}`);

apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts.content: `ipcRenderer.invoke` rejects with a raw Electron `Error` (e.g. `No handler registered for '<channel>'`, main-process crash, or a handler that throws before the router's try/catch wraps it) and that rejection is never normalized to the documented `\`${code}: ${message}\`` shape. Renderers relying on the typed error code (per the file header contract) instead receive an inconsistent generic Electron error message. Normalize the rejection into the typed form.

`api.invoke` is implemented with two parameters `(channel, request)` but cast to the single-parameter type `(request: unknown) => Promise<unknown>`, so the exposed type lies about the arity at the IPC boundary. Additionally, the trailing loop assigns `api[channel]` for every key in `channels`; if any channel key were ever named `invoke`, it would silently overwrite this generic handler. Type the API to accept variadic arguments and build the named handlers without clobbering the generic one.

apps/desktop/src/app/tokens.ts.content: Inconsistent token contract: the status tokens are raw CSS variable references (`var(--ok)` etc.) while every other export in this module is a Tailwind class string. These raw values only work when applied via inline `style` (as `tokenForTone` does in kit.tsx), and passing them to `className` silently applies no colour instead of failing at compile time. Note also that `--ok`/`--warn`/`--bad` are declared in `:root` of styles/globals.css but are never mirrored as `--color-*` inside the `@theme inline` block, so no `text-ok`/`bg-ok` utility exists and these values cannot be used as class strings at all. Consider exposing them as Tailwind theme colours / class strings, or explicitly documenting that these four tokens are raw CSS values for inline styles while all others are class names.

These duplicate existing entries: `fontBody` repeats `type.body` (`text-sm`) and `fontTiming` repeats `type.timing` (`font-timing tabular-nums`). Two independent copies of the same class strings will drift when only one is updated, producing inconsistent typography across components. Alias them to the `type.*` entries (e.g. `export const fontTiming = type.timing;`) or drop the duplicates.

  export const fontTiming = "font-timing tabular-nums";

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/input-gro.content: The internal `onClick` is declared before `{...props}`. Since `props` is the rest of `React.ComponentProps<"div">` (callers' `onClick` is NOT destructured out), any caller-supplied `onClick` is spread last and silently replaces this handler, disabling the addon's click-to-focus behavior. Merge the caller handler with the built-in one instead of letting the spread override it.

`querySelector("input")` only matches `<input>` elements, so an addon placed next to an `InputGroupTextarea` fails to forward focus (the exported textarea subcomponent is never targeted). Prefer selecting the group control via its data-slot (`[data-slot=input-group-control]`) so both input and textarea are handled.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/slider.ts.content: Thumb count is derived from `_values.length`, but `_values` does not reflect what Radix actually manages. When neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is supplied, the memo falls back to `[min, max]`, so this renders 2 Thumbs while `SliderPrimitive.Root` (no `defaultValue` forwarded) defaults to a single value (`[min]`). Radix positions each Thumb by `value[index]`, so the extra Thumb reads `value[1] === undefined` and ends up mis-positioned/NaN. Symmetrically, `value={[]}` renders 0 Thumbs. Either forward a matching `defaultValue`/`value` to the Root, or make the fallback consistent with Radix (single `[min]`).

Nested ternary expression (chained `Array.isArray(...)` conditionals) is explicitly disallowed by the project rules and makes the fallback logic hard to verify. Refactor to early returns inside the memo.

These guards are always true: `min` and `max` have destructuring defaults (`min = 0`, `max = 100`), so `min !== undefined` / `max !== undefined` can never be false. The empty false-branch is dead code and the conditional spread adds noise — forward the props directly.

apps/desktop/src/routes/library/track-ke.content: The disambiguation test only asserts that the two same-title labels are *not equal* (`not.toBe`) rather than checking the deterministic label format the module produces (`<title> - <artist> (<trackId prefix>)`). A broken implementation that appended anything differing per-row (index, random suffix, title duplicated with a counter) would still pass. Also, the two rows here have distinct artists (`"A"`/`"B"`), so an implementation keyed on title+artist would look correct while still colliding when two rows share both title and artist. Add an exact-value assertion and a same-title + same-artist case (with trackIds differing after the 8-char prefix, which is where `libraryRowKey(row).slice(0, 8)` can collide).

This rename-stability case alone cannot prove keying identity: it would also pass if `libraryRowKey` returned a constant (e.g. `"row"`), since both inputs yield the same key. Nothing here asserts that two *different* trackIds produce *different* keys, which is the core contract of `libraryRowKey` (stable, unique React keys). Add an assertion that `libraryRowKey({ trackId: "t2" }) !== libraryRowKey({ trackId: "t1" })`.

Only the empty-string case is exercised for `normalizeTrackId`. Since the implementation `trim()`s before validating, whitespace-only ids (e.g. `"   "`, `"\t"`) also throw and are the realistic invalid case. Tests should cover whitespace-only (and optionally a non-string/null/undefined input) so an implementation that drops trimming or falls back to title for these is caught.

apps/desktop/src/routes/settings/simulat.content: Protocol mismatch: the `simulator/mode` request schema in `packages/ipc/src/index.ts` declares only `{ version, enabled }` (no `scenario`), and the main-process handler calls `setSimulatorMode(req.enabled)` which records/persists only `enabled`. The `scenario` field produced here is therefore not part of the channel contract and is silently stripped by the zod `parse` in the IPC router (unknown keys are dropped by default), so the selected scenario never reaches the backend. A consumer that wires this intent into `invoke` will believe the scenario is transmitted when it is not. Either extend the `simulator/mode` request schema + handler to carry `scenario`, or drop `scenario` from the payload so the intent matches the wire contract.
apps/desktop/src/routes/settings/simulat.existing_code: return { channel: "simulator/mode", payload: { version: 1, enabled: pick.enabled, scenario: pick.scenario } };
